messages.author: 8559f272679693c3
messages.subject: gl.subample.loci error
parts:
Hi all,

 

I'm trying the function gl.subset.loci for the first time and get an error that I don't understand. I'd be grateful for advice.

 

Here are the commands I’ve used and the results…

 

#This is my dataset

Test.pomacentrus

/// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 

// 484 genotypes,  8,306 binary SNPs, size: 2.4 Mb

33031 (0.82 %) missing data

 

// Basic content

   @gen: list of 484 SNPbin

   @ploidy: ploidy of each individual  (range: 2-2)

 

// Optional content

   @ind.names:  484 individual labels

   @loc.names:  8306 locus labels

   @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 2-79)

   @other: a list containing: latlong  Region

 

#Checking it’s formatted OK (created under an older dartR)

> gl.compliance.check(Test.pomacentrus.gl)
Starting gl.compliance.check 
  Processing a SNP dataset
  Checking coding of SNPs
    SNP data scored NA, 0, 1 or 2 confirmed
  Checking locus metrics and flags
  Recalculating locus metrics
  Checking for monomorphic loci
    Dataset containes monomorphic loci
  Checking for individual metrics
    Individual metrics confirmed
  Checking for population assignments
  Population assignments confirmed
Spelling of coordinates checked and changed if necessary
Completed: gl.compliance.check 
 /// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////
 
 // 484 genotypes,  8,306 binary SNPs, size: 3.1 Mb
 33031 (0.82 %) missing data
 
 // Basic content
   @gen: list of 484 SNPbin
   @ploidy: ploidy of each individual  (range: 2-2)
 
 // Optional content
   @ind.names:  484 individual labels
   @loc.names:  8306 locus labels
   @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 2-79)
   @other: a list containing: latlong  Region  loc.metrics  loc.metrics.flags  verbose  history

 

#Run the gl.subsample.loci function

 

> subset3000loci.pomacentrus <- gl.subsample.loci(Test.pomacentrus, n=1000)
Starting gl.subsample.loci 
  Processing a SNP dataset
Error in if (x@other$loc.metrics.flags$monomorphs == FALSE) { : 
  argument is of length zero

 

It seems to be referencing one of the new @other optional contents that were added by gl.compliance.check.

 

I’ve tried including some of the other optional commands (e.g. mono.rm = TRUE) for the function, but no luck.

 

Anybody else encountered this?

 

Cheers,

 

Olly

 

 

http://www.csiro.au/environomics

messages.author: 25b837cc0a77be4e
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.subample.loci error
parts:
Hey Olly,
I haven’t use the function but looking at the function code on github i would guess this issue is that the if statement starting at line 83 should be part of the if(mono.rm) group of if statements starting at line 74. 

You might be able to get around it by assigning the column its looking for to your genlight? Something like:
Test.pomacentrus@other$loc.metrics.flags$monomorphs <- FALSE

-Dale

Sent from the village hidden in the leaves

messages.subject: RE: [dartR] gl.subample.loci error
parts:
Thanks Dale and Renee for your suggestions.

 

I’m embarrassed to say that when I retraced my steps I had no problem running the gl.subsample.loci function, and it worked whether I pre-removed monomorphic loci or included the mono.rm command in gl.subsample.loci.

 

I suspect that there was some minor format problem in my input genlight yesterday that has now been remedied.. The only thing I can think I may have done wrong yesterday is to run the gl.compliance.check function without saving it – i.e. x.gl <- glcompliance.check(x.gl) not just glcompliance.check(x.gl), which I think just reports.

 

In any case…the function is not broken Arthur!

Thanks again…

Cheers,

 

Olly

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.subample.loci error
parts:
Hi Olly,

I would have got to it. Yes, gl.compliance.check takes a genlight object and, by assignment, makes a new compliant genlight object. It is a bummer, but it fixes two problems. 1. the constraints placed on us by CRAN in getting the new dartR compliant with their requirements led to loss of backward compatibility in placed and 2. we did a major overhaul anyway that trashed backward compatibility were it not for the gl.compliance.check script.

All the best, and have a good break.

A
On Tue, 15 Dec 2020 at 19:45, Berry, Olly (NCMI, IOMRC Crawley) <Oliver...@csiro.au> wrote:

Thanks Dale and Renee for your suggestions.

 

I’m embarrassed to say that when I retraced my steps I had no problem running the gl.subsample.loci function, and it worked whether I pre-removed monomorphic loci or included the mono.rm command in gl.subsample.loci.

 

I suspect that there was some minor format problem in my input genlight yesterday that has now been remedied.. The only thing I can think I may have done wrong yesterday is to run the gl.compliance.check function without saving it – i.e. x.gl <- glcompliance.check(x.gl) not just glcompliance.check(x.gl), which I think just reports.
